> **What this case shows** — the [ANOVA](../gait-grf-anova-pathology-gaitrec/index.qmd) and
> [Tukey](../gait-grf-tukey-pathology-gaitrec/index.qmd) siblings compared gait-class *means* of the
> vertical-GRF dynamic range. Do the classes also differ in *variance* — is gait more or less consistent
> with pathology? The **newly-authored** `leveneTest` (robust Brown-Forsythe) says **yes** (F(4,1839)=3.42,
> **p=0.009**), with healthy controls the **most variable** (SD 0.13 vs pathology ~0.11) — while the
> classical, normality-sensitive **Bartlett** test **misses it** (p=0.079). `leveneTest` reproduces
> **`scipy.stats.levene`** and **`car::leveneTest`** to machine precision. Pathology both flattens the GRF
> **and** constrains its variability.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — the grouped feature → `leveneTest(center="median")` → read F and p.
**Way of thinking** — equal-variance is an assumption, not a given; test it, and use the *robust* test
(Brown-Forsythe, median-centred) when the data is skewed. When the robust and classical tests disagree,
trust the robust one — the classical Bartlett is powerful but fragile to non-normality.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioMoCap::grfLandmarks()` (via the sibling), `PhysioAnalysis::leveneTest()`.
:::

## Proposition

The five GaitRec gait classes differ in the variance of their vertical-GRF dynamic range: robust Levene
F(4,1839)=3.42, p=0.0086 (healthy controls most variable), while Bartlett gives p=0.079; `leveneTest`
reproduces `scipy.stats.levene(center='median')` and `car::leveneTest(center=median)` to machine precision.

## Question & goal

**The question is dispersion, and the right test for it: do the classes differ in how variable the dynamic
range is?** The mean-comparison folds assumed equal variance; this fold checks that assumption and asks a new
biological question about the consistency of gait.

## Challenge & approach

We take the same certified per-subject dynamic range for the five classes and run `leveneTest` (Brown-Forsythe,
median-centred) — a one-way ANOVA on the absolute deviations from each class's median — checking F against
`scipy.stats.levene` and `car::leveneTest`, and reporting the classical Bartlett p for contrast.

```
GaitRec dynamic range, 5 classes (n=1844) → leveneTest (center=median)
  per-class SD:  HC 0.128 > K 0.115 ~ H 0.115 > C 0.110 ~ A 0.109
  Levene (robust)    F(4,1839) = 3.42,  p = 0.0086   -> variances DIFFER
  Bartlett (classical)             p = 0.079    -> not significant (disagrees!)
     vs scipy.stats.levene(center=median)  → |diff| ~ 1e-14
     vs car::leveneTest(center=median)     → |diff| ~ 1e-14
```

## Data

**GaitRec (Horsak et al. 2020)**: the vertical-GRF dynamic range for the five gait classes — healthy control
(n=208), ankle (n=483), knee (n=499), hip (n=364), calcaneus (n=290). Same cohort as the ANOVA/Tukey
siblings. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: per-class SD of the dynamic range — healthy controls are the most variable (0.13 BW), the four pathology classes tighter (~0.11). Right: the two variance tests — the robust Levene clears the p=0.05 line (p=0.009) while the classical Bartlett does not (p=0.079). They disagree.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* left — pathology not only lowers the mean dynamic range (earlier folds) but tightens its
spread. Right — the choice of variance test matters: the robust Levene detects the heterogeneity the
normality-sensitive Bartlett misses.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **Levene F** (df 4, 1839) | **3.42** (p = 0.0086) |
| Bartlett p (classical) | 0.079 (ns) |
| healthy / pathology SD | 0.128 / ~0.11 |
| n | 1844 |
| vs `scipy.stats.levene` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~1e-14) |
| vs `car::leveneTest` (\|diff\|) | **< 1e-9** (~1e-14) |

The F equals both references to machine precision. Values trace to
[`artifacts/levene_summary.csv`](artifacts/levene_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`leveneTest` reproduces the reference on the certified dynamic range. The transferable takeaway: **test
equal-variance with the robust Levene, not just the classical Bartlett — here they disagree, and the robust
test wins. Biologically, impaired gait is not only flatter but more stereotyped: the pathology classes vary
less than healthy controls, a floor effect on an already-flattened force profile.**

## Open questions

- Levene and Bartlett disagree because the dynamic range is non-normal (Bartlett is sensitive to that); the
  lower pathology variance may be a floor effect, which a joint location-scale model would separate from a
  genuine consistency difference. The single robust Levene test is the standard first-line variance check.
  *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| GRF landmarks (dynamic range) | `grfLandmarks()` | PhysioMoCap |
| Homogeneity of variance (robust) | `leveneTest()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| One-way ANOVA (means) | `oneWayAnova()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **center = "median"** — the Brown-Forsythe variant, robust to non-normality; prefer it over the
  mean-centred classic Levene and over Bartlett when the data may be skewed.
- **disagreement** — if Bartlett and Levene conflict, suspect non-normality and report the robust Levene.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

leveneTest(list(HC = hc_dr, Ankle = a_dr, Knee = k_dr, Hip = h_dr, Calcaneus = c_dr), center = "median")
# F, p, df -- machine precision vs scipy.stats.levene and car::leveneTest  (use PhysioAnalysis:: if car is attached)
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/levene_summary.csv`](artifacts/levene_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
Levene F, its p and df, the machine-precision match against scipy and car, the robust-vs-classical
disagreement with Bartlett, the healthy-most-variable pattern, the sample size, and the honestly noted scope
(authors the new leveneTest op; dynamic range from the certified grfLandmarks; Bartlett for contrast only;
cross-sectional association).
